text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code easier to read and understand, which helps both current team members and future developers. When you refactor, the software should behave exactly as before, so users do not notice any difference. Good refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design decisions pile up over time. By cleaning up messy code regularly, teams can keep their projects healthy and make future changes faster and safer.
